rows: processors +50% faster (two at most: +100%), for more RF per operation, and heat

pages.text:
**Overclocking.** An Overclock Bay makes every processor on the machine faster, at a price: each operation costs a quarter more RF, and each working processor heats the machine. A machine sheds a little heat by itself; cold blocks against its open sides (snow, ice, packed or blue ice) take much more. When the heat reaches 1,000 the machine **overheats** and works at normal speed until it is down to 300. Jade shows the heat.

One overclocked processor in still air overheats after about half a minute. One ice block keeps it running; blue ice keeps two.

Use an upgrade on a chassis to fill the first free bay; remove one from the configurator. Removal is **refused** if it would no longer fit what is stored: empty the lane, reservoir or buffer first. Upgrades never add faces or functions.
